summary: Stale and superseded: the change edits wg2_kernel at OCC2 / G=264 on the restack-occ2-wg2-b256 base, but that base never landed (it is on FINDINGS' Do-not-try list), master's submission.py has no wg2 kernel, and verify_32 now runs a hybrid (hot experts on the OCC1 wg_kernel, cold experts on Engine A ea4, on two concurrent streams). Even if it were re-aimed at that hybrid, the plausible headline gain is about 0.1-0.4%, well under the 1.24% bar, and the change is expensive and high-risk.
justification: A. The premise is a persistent wg2 grid of G = 2 x 132 = 264 CTAs whose last wave leaves G - r CTAs idle. That kernel does not exist on master (2ec8090f, board 1.8941). grep finds no wg2 symbol in muse_moe_w4a16/submission.py. The only wgmma GEMM is wg_kernel, with __launch_bounds__(THREADS, 1) and state['wg_grid'] = multi_processor_count (G=132, OCC1). The hypothesis's depends_on, restack-occ2-wg2-b256-two-stream-halves-on-master, measured neutral within-ci and sits on the Do-not-try list. The campaign's own wg2 hot half (H=-17, LOG 2026-10-27T0131Z/0136Z) was killed on both moe (x0.405 at T=128, x0.882 at T=256) and decode, and SINGLE-PASS.md lists 'wg2 re-split' as dead. Master routes bs=256 (verify_32, 304.5 us scored, floor 108.9) through _hm_forward with H=-16. Per the board profile 0b49b1aa, profile 5, wg_kernel<true> handles the hot experts in 63.6 us and wg_kernel<false> in 64.4 us, on a fork stream concurrent with ea4_w13 (141.2 us) and ea4_w2 (113.5 us). That is 400.9 us of kernel time against 307.5 us of GPU-busy time, so the two halves overlap heavily. The weakest link: 'idle tail CTAs' no longer means idle SMs. When the hot half's last wave is partial, the concurrent cold Engine A CTAs fill those SMs, so recovering the hot-half tail mostly shifts work rather than shortening the makespan. The critical path is the ea4 cold chain (~255 us), not the 128 us hot chain. The stated expectation was already only +0.2-0.9% headline on a 358 us verify_32 that no longer exists. On today's 304 us row, with the tail hidden behind the cold stream, a realistic figure is 0-5 us, i.e. under 0.3% geomean from one of six loads. The prior check is also weak. The difference from wg-stream-k-tail-split (held) was 'G=264 wg2 instead of G=132 wg_kernel', and master has gone back to the G=132 wg_kernel, now in a different role (hot-only, concurrent). The campaign also measured a ticket/last-arriver tail directly: W6-A, LOG 0728Z, cost about twice what it saved, and the lesson recorded there is 'no single-CTA tails'. Only the fixed-order fp32 partial sum differs from that design.
confounders: campaign X2 / W6-M fork hybrid (hm, H=-16, landed 72e6bd6d / 86e4a4d9): the wgmma hot half now runs on a fork stream concurrent with the Engine A cold half, so any tail recovery on wg_kernel is absorbed by SM sharing with ea4. A measured gain or loss at bs=256 would reflect co-scheduling with the cold stream, not tail utilization.

campaign Engine A ea4 (cold half at T=256; L3/L4/X1 decode tweaks through 2ec8090f): ea4_w13 + ea4_w2 (~255 us) is the longer stream and so sets verify_32's makespan; shortening the hot half below it does not move the row.
wg-pdl-gather-w13-w2-chain (landed neutral): PDL on the w13->w2 boundary already overlaps w2's ramp with w13's tail; the hypothesis itself flags this, and it compounds the attribution problem.
restack-occ2-wg2-b256-two-stream-halves-on-master (Do-not-try, never landed): the named base is absent, so the change cannot be built as written.
interference: No companions. The hypothesis cannot be built as specified because its kernel and base are absent. A companion would only make sense for a re-aimed version on the hm hot half's wg_kernel. Even then, a fork-stream-serialized control (the hot half run without the concurrent cold stream) would be needed to see any tail effect at all. That costs an extra check to resolve a gain capped well under 1.24%, which the user's bar rules out.
rules_flags: No hard rule violation in the design (per-state workspace, fp32 partials summed in fixed slice order, no host sync, no input-derived caching).

Correctness hazard, not a rules issue: 'counter zeroed by the kernel's own prologue for the next replay' races with same-launch atomicAdds unless the zeroing is ordered before any CTA reaches the tail. The usual safe pattern is for the last arriver to reset its own item's ticket after it consumes the partials. Graph-replay corruption would show up as a judge recheck failure (cf. s3's rel-L2 1.21 on repetition 2).
open_questions: If anyone wants to revive the tail idea, the target is the H=-16 hot half's wg_kernel at G=132. First measure how much of its last wave is actually uncovered by the concurrent ea4 cold stream (prepare-time graph timing with and without the fork). If the uncovered tail is under ~4 us at T=256, drop the idea.
Is there evidence that the verify_32 makespan is ever bound by the hot half rather than the ea4 cold chain under the judge routing? If not, nothing in the hot half's decomposition can move the row.
